q: A design team is evaluating glazing options for a corporate tower located directly beside an elevated railway line. The client reports persistent low-frequency vibration noise entering the interior spaces, especially during peak train hours. The facade consultant specifies that the chosen glass must improve the building's STC rating without significantly increasing overall glass thickness, and it must also function as safety glazing for a high-rise exterior. During testing, several glass types are reviewed, but only one option demonstrates the ability to dampen vibration, reduce resonance between glass layers, and maintain the impact-resistant performance required by code. Which glazing type best satisfies all of these requirements?
o: Insulated Glass Unit (IGU) with Air Gap
n: Acoustic laminated glass has a special damping interlayer. It raises STC, reduces resonance between plies, and remains safety glazing. Source: ASTM E90/E413 (STC); ASTM C1172.

q: A popular observation deck is being designed to extend from the 42nd floor of a mixed-use tower, allowing tourists to step onto a transparent glass platform and look straight down to the street below. The walkable glass surface must withstand heavy foot traffic, unpredictable crowd loads, and the possibility of objects being dropped by visitors. The design brief requires the glass to remain intact even if one or more plies fracture, ensuring that no tourist is placed at risk during a post-breakage event. The platform must also limit deflection to avoid discomfort for visitors who may be sensitive to movement at high elevation. Which glazing assembly best satisfies these requirements?
o: Double-glazed IGU with tempered outer lite
n: Walkable glass floors use triple laminated glass. The extra plies give strength, stiffness and redundancy, so the floor stays intact if one or two plies break. Source: IStructE, Structural Use of Glass in Buildings; ASTM E2751.

q: Modern glazing technologies help improve thermal efficiency. UV protection and indoor comfort without compromising clarity. Some specialized glass types feature invisible coatings that regulate heat transfer and prevent excessive solar gain. Which of the following is designed to reduce heat loss in cold climates and minimize heat gain in warm climates while maintaining maximum optical transparency?
n: Low-E glass has a nearly invisible metal-oxide coating that limits radiant heat transfer, cutting heat loss or gain while staying highly transparent. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing) (low-emissivity coatings).

q: Glass in elevator hoistway enclosures, elevator car enclosures, elevator car doors. Glass floors as a walking surface
n: Elevator hoistway and car enclosures, car doors and walkable glass floors require laminated glass. Source: ASME A17.1, Sec. 2.11/2.14 (glass in elevators); IBC 2409.

q: Which glass is used for display eases when clarity is of main concern?
n: Low-iron (extra-clear) glass has almost no green tint, giving maximum clarity for display cases. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing).

q: Which glass is used for display cases when security is of main concern?
n: Laminated glass resists break-ins and holds together, so it is used for display cases where security matters. Source: ASTM F1233.

q: Which glass is used for display cases when strength and safety 1s of main concern?
n: Tempered glass is about four times stronger than annealed and breaks into safe granules, so it suits cases where strength and safety matter. Source: ASTM C1048.

q: Which glass is used for display cases when you want them to be budget-friendly?
n: Ordinary annealed glass is the cheapest option for display cases. Source: ASTM C1048 (heat-treated glass) / ASTM C1172 (laminated glass); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing).

q: Which glass ts used for car windshields?
n: Windshields are laminated: the interlayer holds the glass together on impact. Source: ANSI Z26.1 (automotive safety glazing).

q: Which glass is used for the car's passenger and rear windows?
n: Side and rear car windows are usually tempered glass, which crumbles into small pieces. Source: ANSI Z26.1.

q: Glass created by mixing various ingredients, melting them and then pouring it on a molten tin bath on which molten glass flows to form a very flat glass surface with uniform thickness.
n: Float glass is made by floating molten glass on a bath of molten tin, which gives a very flat surface and uniform thickness. Source: ASTM C1036 (Flat Glass); Pilkington float process.

q: A curtain wall contractor is reviewing the glazing schedule for a high-rise tower. As the elevation increases, the facade is exposed to stronger wind pressures and greater deflection demands. The consultant notes that the glass specification for upper floors must be adjusted to resist higher wind loads, limit excessive flexing, and maintain occupant comfort during strong gusts. Which option best satisfies the requirement for glass used on higher floors?
n: Higher floors see higher wind pressure. Thicker glass (or more plies) is specified to resist the load and limit deflection. Source: ASTM E1300 (glass load resistance); NSCP 2015, Sec. 207 (wind pressure increases with height).

q: In modern architectural glazing systems. structural reinforcement is necessary to support expansive glass panels while maintaining minimal visual obstruction, Various methods are used to ensure stability, with some relying on rigid vertical stabilizers integrated into the glass structures. Others use mechanical fasteners or tension-based elements to hold panels in place. Which option offers the most effective rigid stabilization while preserving a sleek frameless aesthetic?
n: Glass fins are rigid vertical stabilizers behind the panels. They brace large glazing against wind without frames. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems) (fin-supported glazing).

q: When designing a frameless glazing system for a three-meter-wide glass installation, structural stability is crucial to manage load distribution while maintaining optical clarity. Various attachment methods exist. ranging from surface- mounted fittings to tension-based anchoring. Which of the following is the most effective point-load transfer mechanism for securing large-format glass panels without compromising structural integrity?
n: Spider fittings are multi-arm point supports that carry large glass panels at their corners back to the structure. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems) (point-supported glazing).

q: A luxury electric-vehicle showroom in a newly developed commercial district is designed with a dramatic cantilevered steel canopy that extends over a frameless glass facade. The architect wants the glass panels to appear as if they are floating, with no visible mullions, while still being securely connected to the structural steel arms supporting the canopy. The connection system must allow point-supported glazing, accommodate slight building movements, and maintain a clean, high-end aesthetic suitable for premium automotive branding. Which hardware best meets these requirements?
o: Aluminum pressure plate curtain wall system
n: Spider fittings give point-supported, mullion-free glass that seems to float, connected to steel arms and allowing slight movement. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems).

q: Which of the following is specifically designed for point-fixed glass assemblies, often used in curtain walls and facades 1o connect glass panels with minimal framing?
n: Spider fittings are designed for point-fixed glass assemblies with minimal framing. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems).

q: Frameless glass railing systems require specialized fastening methods to provide both structural stability and aesthetic continuity. Some systems offer continuous base support, while others rely on discrete mounting points to achieve a sleek, floating effect. Which of the following solutions offers the most effective point-fixed method for securing glass balusters while maintaining a minimalist design?
n: Glass standoffs bolt through each baluster panel to the slab edge or stringer, a point-fixed look with no base channel. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems) (frameless glass railings); IBC 2407.

q: A luxury retail storefront requires oversized glass panels to align flush with a concealed steel header and floor beam, producing a perfectly continuous facade with no exposed point hardware. The system must restrain the glass along its entire edge to control lateral drift from foot-traffic-induced vibration, while keeping all anchorage fully hidden to preserve the brand's minimalist aesthetic. Which component best satisfies these performance and visual requirements?
n: A concealed U-channel holds the glass along its whole edge at the header and floor, with no exposed point hardware. Source: GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems).

q: A boutique facade uses oversized monolithic glass panels arranged edge-to-edge to maintain uninterrupted optical continuity. The design requires the joint to absorb differential movement between panels, and demands a bond line that remains nearly invisible under both daylight and artificial lighting. Which material best satisfies these performance requirements for the glass-to-glass interface?
n: Clear (structural or weather) silicone at butt joints absorbs movement and is nearly invisible. Source: ASTM C1184 (structural silicone sealants); GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems).

q: In glazing systems, what is the primary function of structural sealant?
o: To provide a continuous vapor barrier across curtain wall transitions
To bond glass to supporting substrates while transferring lateral loads without mechanical fasteners
'To isolate thermal bridges between glass panels and adjacent framing elements
To prevent moisture migration within multi-pane insulated glazing units
n: Structural silicone bonds glass to its frame and transfers wind loads without mechanical fasteners. Source: ASTM C1401 (Structural Sealant Glazing).

q: In a captured curtain wall system, which component mechanically secures glass panels against the mullions and transoms before the exterior cover cap is installed?
n: In a captured curtain wall, the pressure plate clamps the glass to the mullions and transoms before the cover cap snaps on. Source: AAMA Curtain Wall Manual; GANA Glazing Manual; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (glazing systems).

q: In a curtain wall system, which component is primarily intended to accommodate thermal expansion, interstory drift, and facade movement without transferring excessive stress to the glazing?
n: Sealant joints absorb thermal movement, interstory drift and facade movement without overstressing the glass. Source: ASTM C1472 (joint movement); AAMA Curtain Wall Manual.

q: In the context of shower glass enclosures, what is the primary function of silicone sealant?
o: To provide a flexible, watertight seal between glass and adjacent surfaces, preventing leakage and accommodating movement
To insulate the enclosure thermally and reduce condensation on glass surfaces
To permanently fix the glass panels in place, eliminating the need for mechanical clamps or channels
To structurally bond the glass panels to the wall substrate and support vertical loads
n: In shower enclosures, silicone gives a flexible, watertight seal between the glass and adjacent surfaces. It is not structural. Source: GANA Glazing Manual (shower enclosures).

q: Best material for floor of a warehouse
n: Concrete slab floors suit warehouses because they take forklift traffic and heavy loads. Source: ACI 302.1R (Guide to Concrete Floor and Slab Construction).

q: From among the choices, which is the most appropriate floor finish for a workshop?
n: Plain cement plaster (steel-troweled concrete) is durable and cheap for workshops. Source: ACI 302.1R; Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: From among the choices, which are the most appropriate floor tiles for an open deck?
n: Open decks need non-skid (slip-resistant) tiles for wet exterior use. Source: ANSI A137.1 / A326.3 (DCOF slip resistance).

q: If low maintenance and ease of replacement are prime considerations for a high- end project, which flooring would you specify?
n: Luxury carpet tiles combine a high-end look with low maintenance, and damaged tiles can be swapped one at a time. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (floor finishes); manufacturer data; CRI (Carpet and Rug Institute).

q: Which type of resilient flooring offers high water resistance, excellent durability, and is easier to install than natural stone or tile, making it ideal for high-traffic or wet areas like gyms and hospitals?
n: Rubber flooring resists water, is very durable and installs more easily than stone or tile. It is ideal for gyms and hospitals. Source: ASTM F1859/F1860 (rubber flooring).

q: Which flooring material provides the highest impact protection for active play rooms and is commonly specified in thicknesses from 15 mm to 50 mm?
n: Rubber tiles or rolls, 15–50 mm thick, give the most impact protection in active play and gym areas. Source: ASTM F1292 (impact attenuation of surfacing).

q: Which of the following lists the primary raw materials used to make traditional linoleum?
o: Linseed oil, pine resin, cork dust, wood flour, calcium carbonate, jute backing
n: Traditional linoleum is linseed oil, pine resin, cork dust, wood flour and calcium carbonate on a jute backing. Source: ASTM F2034 (linoleum sheet).

q: Which flooring material is most suitable for high-impact zones in fitness centers due to its superior shock absorption, slip resistance, and ability to withstand dropped weights?
n: Rubber flooring absorbs shock, resists slipping and takes dropped weights, so it suits fitness high-impact zones. Source: ASTM F2772 (sports floor performance); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (floor finishes); manufacturer data.

q: Which flooring material is preferred for professional indoor basketball courts due to its consistent ball bounce, surface uniformity, and ability to support athlete performance?
n: Professional indoor basketball courts use maple hardwood for consistent ball bounce and uniform surface. Source: MFMA (Maple Flooring Manufacturers Association); FIBA Official Basketball Rules (playing court).

q: Which of the following is considered a green flooring material due to its natural composition, biodegradability, and low environmental impact?
n: Linoleum is natural, biodegradable and low-impact, a green flooring. Source: ASTM F2034; USGBC LEED material credits.

q: Which of the following would you specify if the client wants to use renewable materials with resilience also a prime consideration?
n: Cork is renewable (bark harvested without felling the tree) and resilient. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (floor finishes); manufacturer data.

q: Which facility is appropriate for rubber flooring?
n: Rubber flooring suits sports halls for its shock absorption, slip resistance and durability. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (floor finishes); manufacturer data.

q: It refers to steel beams which can tightly interlock with other beams through slots or indentation.
n: Coped beams have notches or slots cut so they interlock tightly with other beams. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, 15th ed., Part 9 (Coped Beams).

q: Steel beams are designed to support loads by resisting bending and shear forces. However, when exposed to high stress concentrations or localized buckling, additional reinforcements may be required to maintain structural stability. Which of the following components is primarily used to strengthen beams by preventing web buckling and distributing concentrated loads?
n: Stiffeners are welded to the web to prevent web buckling and spread concentrated loads. Source: AISC 360-16, Sec. J10 (Flanges and Webs with Concentrated Forces).

q: A structural steel column is connected to a reinforced concrete pedestal. Which component is primarily used to prevent uplift and separation of the steel column from the concrete foundation?
n: Anchor bolts (anchor rods) tie the column base plate to the pedestal and resist uplift and separation. Source: AISC Design Guide 1 (Base Plate and Anchor Rod Design).

q: A steel column base plate is to be anchored to a concrete pedestal. Which type of anchor bolt has a hooked end specifically designed to improve mechanical anchorage and resistance against pull-out?
n: J-bolts have a hooked end that gives mechanical anchorage against pull-out in cast concrete. Source: AISC Design Guide 1; ACI 318, Ch. 17 (hooked anchors).

q: A contractor needs to fasten a steel bracket to an existing reinforced concrete wall. The anchorage must be installed after the concrete has already hardened and should develop its holding capacity through mechanical expansion within the drilled hole. Which fastening device is most appropriate for this application?
n: Expansion bolts are post-installed in drilled holes in hardened concrete and grip by mechanical expansion. Source: ACI 355.2 (post-installed mechanical anchors).

q: A contractor is installing a frameless glass canopy on an existing reinforced concrete facade. The support brackets must be attached after the concrete has already cured, and the anchorage system must provide high pull-out resistance while minimizing expansion stresses that could crack the concrete. Which fastening system is most appropriate?
n: Chemical (epoxy) anchors are post-installed with high pull-out resistance. They bond without expansion stresses that could crack the concrete. Source: ACI 355.4 (post-installed adhesive anchors).

q: A steel-framed commercial building is scheduled under a fast-track construction program. If speed of erection and ease of site installation are the primary considerations, which connection method is most appropriate?
n: Bolted connections are fastest and easiest to install on site, which suits fast-track erection. Field welding is slower and needs more inspection. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, 15th ed., Part 7 (bolts); AISC Code of Standard Practice.

q: Predominant supplier of steel bars
n: SteelAsia is the predominant local manufacturer and supplier of steel reinforcing bars. Source: SteelAsia Manufacturing Corporation company profile; DTI-BPS PNS 49 licensees.

q: Which is a local manufacturer of steel reinforcement bars?
n: SteelAsia Manufacturing Corporation is a local maker of steel reinforcing bars. Source: DTI-BPS PNS 49 licensees.

q: What is the primary purpose of a diaphragm in a building structural system?
o: To reduce concrete shrinkage and thermal cracking
To serve as a permanent formwork for floor construction
To transfer lateral loads to shear walls and other vertical resisting elements
To support only vertical gravity loads from beams and columns
n: A diaphragm transfers lateral loads to the shear walls and other vertical resisting elements. Source: NSCP 2015, Sec. 208.7; ASCE 7-16, Sec. 12.10.

q: What size of stec! bars is usually used for a residential column main bars
n: 16 mm bars are typical main bars for residential columns. Source: Local residential structural practice; NSCP 2015, Sec. 410.6 (minimum longitudinal steel ratio).

q: Another name for a C-Section Steel Member
n: A C-section is also called a parallel flange channel (PFC). Source: BS EN 10365 (hot-rolled channels); AISC Steel Construction Manual, 15th ed., Part 1.

q: Which steel section is used for Pile Driving?
n: HP-shapes (bearing piles) are used for driven steel piles. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, 15th ed., Part 1 (HP Shapes).
